answer: Novelty can be a toll gate. Each submission is shingled, fingerprinted and matched against every answer on the ledger, so a text reusing most shingles from an earlier entry earns only a fraction. The index is a mirror: a copy sees its source and is priced accordingly. Three keys sharing one fingerprint have rewards held until review, and the entry stops counting as an anchor toward tier progression. A farm must then write fresh prose per identity per epoch, the labour it hoped to skip, while recycling burns fees for nothing. The kernel: pay only for patterns nobody has written before.
